gen-dafont-visitor-gf-kufam: Wide-mouthed e's and stubby ascenders give Visitor a nostalgic grin, as if strokes were pulled through a nozzle. Kufam brings the opposite strength: one tube-like track width and open curves that keep a line of sans-serif text clean.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-liter: Liter reads modern and businesslike, with uniform strokes and a lowercase that stands up proud on the line. But Visitor brings the nostalgic, digital flavor: short ascenders over big bowls, and an e with a gaping mouth.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-matangi: Nostalgic and digital, Visitor pulls its strokes like solder through a nozzle, with gaping e mouths and short ascenders. Matangi's hefty, open-curved lowercase gives that quirk something sturdy to lean on.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-michroma: Nostalgic and digital: Visitor makes every diagonal as stout as every upright, with short ascenders over big bowls. Michroma goes wide instead, giving each letter generous side room and open curves for a contemporary line.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Nostalgic digital charm: Visitor has gaping e mouths and short ascenders sitting above big bowls. Mochiy Pop P One then keeps paragraphs friendly, its wide letter spacing and sizable lowercase making sans-serif text feel approachable.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-mozilla-text: Mozilla Text reads sturdy, its lowercase bodies filling most of the line while terminals flare outward. Visitor adds a nostalgic, digital punch with every stroke at uniform visual weight.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-nata-sans: Nostalgic digital charm up top, discipline underneath. Visitor pulls gaping-mouthed e's and short ascenders over big bowls, while Nata Sans keeps its curves wide open with a technical-pen steadiness.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-nokora: Nostalgic and digital, Visitor feels cut from rod stock. Nokora is the counterpoint, an approachable sans-serif whose wide-open s never tightens and whose dense, dark lowercase fills each line.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans: Nostalgic, digital Visitor gives its s a spine matching its terminals. Noto Sans then carries the paragraphs, its lowercase filling most of the letter height and its open c keeping sentences flowing.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam reads clean and open, its curve endings held well apart. Its full-standing c, s and z mean the text can drop to a modest size, while Visitor supplies the nostalgic, digital edge.
